description: Machine-checkable verification probes: one entry per GitHub issue whose resolution (or regression) is observable from flight telemetry. Evaluated by an agent after (or during) a flight against the session event log and the CMTrace app log — see docs/agents/flight-verification.md for the workflow, sources and reporting rules. Probes are evidence-gatherers: a passing probe means 'observed working this flight', never 'auto-close'.

sources.session: JSONL session event log (sessions/session-*.jsonl): one JSON object per line with timestamp, type, payload.
sources.log: CMTrace application log (logs/ProsimCompanion-*.log): component, level (type 1=info 2=warn 3=error), message.
sources.wire: GSX wire trace (logs/ProsimCompanion-wire-*.log): only consulted when a probe names it; often disabled or huge.

machine: Optional per-probe block for the support reducer (tools/ProsimCompanion.Reduce, docs/agents/support-bundle.md). A probe WITH it is evaluated deterministically; one without is handed to the LLM step untouched. kind=signature: {source: session|log, type?: <event type>, contains: <literal>, component?: <log component>, minCount?: 1} as signature (the failure/behaviour) and, for assert-present, trigger (omitted = always). kind=required-fields: every event of type carries each dotted path in fields; optional where {path: text} checks only the events that read that text at the path, optional fieldsWhenPresent {path: [fields]} requires the fields only on events that carry the path. kind=duplicate-within: no two events of type share key within windowSeconds. kind=consecutive-duplicates: no event of type repeats its predecessor payload.

kinds.assert-absent: The failure signature must NOT appear. Pass = absent all session; fail = present (quote the evidence).
kinds.assert-present: The fixed/feature behaviour must appear WHEN its trigger occurred. Pass = trigger+behaviour seen; not-exercised = trigger never occurred (report as untested, not passed); fail = trigger seen without the behaviour.
kinds.watch: Health signal with no fixed pass/fail: count and report occurrences with context.
kinds.feature-pending: Issue is an unimplemented feature; probe documents what to assert once it ships. Skip during evaluation, but report accidental sightings.
kinds.requires-human: Not observable from telemetry (web UI, audio quality, installer). Listed so the flight report can remind the pilot what to eyeball.

checks: Only with sayIntentions.arrivalGateFromAtc = true (off by default). Trigger = SayIntentions' flight.json assigned_gate changing after takeoff (ATC reassigns, or 'taxi to gate …' after landing).

assert-present: a 'sayintentions.arrival-gate' event with decision QueueArrival naming that gate, followed by the arrival-gate coordinator's log line 'Arrival gate <gate> assigned by SayIntentions ATC (<phase>) — sending to GSX now | queued for cruise', then the normal GSX gate.select ladder (gsx-gate-resolved / gsx-gate-not-found).

assert-present: on the ground before takeoff a DepartureGateNoted decision for the departure stand, and no QueueArrival for that same text later in the flight (SameAsDeparture is the correct decision while SI still shows it).

assert-absent: a QueueArrival while the pilot had already queued a gate on the OFP page (PilotGateWins is the correct decision); any assignGate call to SayIntentions for a gate that came FROM SayIntentions (the ATC status line reads 'Assigned by SayIntentions ATC — nothing to send back').

watch: when does SayIntentions actually change assigned_gate on arrival — on approach or only after landing? Note the phase of the QueueArrival; after landing the gate goes to GSX at once and gate.select must still be accepted (not PARKED).
requires-human: GSX parked the aircraft at the gate ATC named.
probes.notes: Feature 2026-10-08 (Open-items batch, no issue number; unverified live). AtcAssignedGateRule (Core, pure) + SayIntentionsArrivalGateSource (Speech) + ArrivalGateCoordinator.ConfirmFromAtc. The departure stand is remembered because flight.json carries ONE assigned_gate for the whole flight.

checks: Every 'sayintentions.request' event now carries radioWaitMs and radioBusyAtTx. With MSFS connected: radioWaitMs ≥ 400 and, when ATC was mid-sentence as the pilot asked, visibly longer (up to 8000). Without MSFS: exactly the ~400 ms fallback.

watch: radioBusyAtTx = true means the gate gave up after 8 s and transmitted into a busy frequency — count them and note whether SIAI_COM1_RECEIVING really was 1 the whole time (a stuck L:var would show as every request busy).
watch: the log line 'Radio-clear gate: SIAI L:var subscription failed' — the gate is off for the session; report once.
requires-human: the FO's transmission no longer steps on the end of an ATC sentence; and a long ATC monologue does not make the FO wait more than ~8 s.
probes.notes: Feature 2026-10-08 (Phase 5 leftover closed; unverified live). RadioClearGate over L:SIAI_COM1_RECEIVING / L:SIAI_RADIO_PTT through ISimVars (SayIntentionsLvarNames). The sim auto-creates an unknown L:var as 0, so a SayIntentions that never writes them reads 'clear' — the predecessor's degrade.

checks: At startup one 'Wake-on-LAN magic packet sent to <MAC> via <broadcast>:<port>' log line per enabled row of wakeOnLan.targets; a config still carrying briefing.llmWakeOnLan enabled additionally logs 'briefing.llmWakeOnLan is the old single-PC form — open Settings → Setup → Wake-on-LAN once to move it into the list'.
requires-human: after the first visit to Settings → Setup the old LLM row appears in the list and the dirty bar asks to save; after that save the legacy log line is gone on the next start.
requires-human: 'Send now' on a row wakes that PC; 'Wake PCs' on the Voice FO status section wakes them all.
probes.notes: Owner idea 2026-10-08: one list of PCs instead of a switch per feature. WakeTargetsOptions / WakeOnLanStartup in Core; the Speech project's LlmWakeOnLanStartup is gone.

checks: Trigger = a 'sayintentions.frequency-assigned' event (station, khz, source Handoff|CorrectFrequency|unknown) between pushback and taxi-in. One is expected after every ATC hand-off; list them all with their times and compare with what ATC said — a hand-off with NO matching event within ~30 s means the 'Contact … on …' wording was not read (quote the SayIntentions message if the pilot has it).

assert-present: when the pilot deliberately left COM1 on another frequency for longer than sayIntentions.frequencyMonitorWaitSeconds (default 60), exactly one 'fo.wrong-frequency-advisory' event with assignedKhz = the last assignment and com1Khz = what the radio was on, and the log line 'Wrong-frequency report: COM1 on … kHz, assigned … kHz'.

assert-absent: a second 'fo.wrong-frequency-advisory' with the same assignedKhz AND com1Khz without COM1 having returned to the assignment in between; any advisory while the phase was ColdAndDark / Preflight / Departure / Shutdown; any advisory within the wait after a new 'sayintentions.frequency-assigned'.

watch: every advisory the pilot did NOT expect is a false alarm — report it with the assignment event before it and its source. source CorrectFrequency (before the first hand-off) is the least proven path: report what SayIntentions named and whether it was right.
watch: 'SayIntentions assigned frequency unknown' log lines — each is an unreadable hand-off or 90 s without a successful getCommsHistory poll; count them.
requires-human: the FO line 'Captain, we should be on <station>, <digits>.' is heard once, names the right station, and does not talk over an ATC exchange.
probes.notes: Feature (owner request 2026-10-05, no issue number; unverified live). SayIntentionsFrequencyMonitor: ProSim COM1 active vs the last 'Contact … on …' of getCommsHistory (correct_frequency of getCurrentFrequencies only before the first hand-off). Checks at all times SI is in use, copilot on or off (owner Option A). Reply shapes and the two traps (SI accepts a wrong station; the frequencies[] list is the nearest airport's) are in docs/integrations/sayintentions.md. Not yet seen live: arrival and FAA hand-off wording, since_id behaviour.

checks: No 'phase-changed' event into InitialClimb/Climb/Cruise/Descent/Approach whose snapshot has iasKt < 30 AND groundSpeedKt < 30 (with #93 shipped, also onGround=true or powered=false — physically impossible airborne states).

No log line 'GSX "fob restore": ... -> ... (saved value)' before the session has a genuine airborne phase commit (ias > 80 at the transition). The refusal line ('refused — aircraft has not been airborne') is the CORRECT behaviour.
No 'aircraft-state-check' skipped with reason 'already airborne this session' in a session that never actually flew.

assert-present when ProSim connects after the app started: a 'Flight phase classification suspended ... plausible: False' log line during connection warm-up (the plausibility gate doing its job), followed by 'enabled ... plausible: True' once real data arrives.
Any 'airborne-this-session latch withheld' log line is the hardened latch refusing weak evidence — expected on artifacts, report it with its snapshot fields.
probes.notes: Fixed in three layers (2026-08-22): physical-plausibility gate (airborne at <30 kt IAS AND GS = hold Unknown), airborne latch requires convincing evidence (ias>=80 or RA>=200 at commit), Unknown->airborne commits carry a 5 s first-classification debounce. The definitive live test remains: start the app, then start ProSim, and confirm no bogus phase, no FOB restore, and the state check still runs.

checks: If a 'gsx-decision' with reason containing 'waiting for a flight plan' exists, no 'gsx-service' {service: Refueling, event: Active} may occur before a later decision shows the plan was detected (simbriefImported=True or fmsOrigin non-empty in the 'flight plan detection' decision).
probes.notes: The OFP gate only holds the automation path; GSX-side requests bypass it. Fail = fuel/boarding ran planless.

checks: Between 'gsx-service' {Boarding, Requested} and {Boarding, Completed}, at most 2 distinct passenger counts across 'gsx-decision' events with action 'pax target' (reason contains 'armed GSX with N passengers').
probes.notes: 2026-08-16 flight thrashed 89→91→88→85→91→89 from SimBrief pax randomization re-imports during boarding.

checks: When the anchor runs: a 'gate anchor: anchored GSX to 'X' (code)' decision — and REPORT WHICH ladder rung X was (display name, full facility|gate key, bglName, or bare designator): which identity gate.select matches on is the open empirical question this probe answers.
assert-absent: 'gate.select failed for every identity [...]' — the whole ladder refused means a genuinely unknown-to-GSX stand (cross-check the #44 probe).
Arrival selects at decorated stands ('Stand 547 with Safedock©') accept the unambiguous designator match instead of refusing.
probes.notes: Fixed 2026-08-22: the anchor walks an identity ladder (not_found advances, any other code stops) and nearest-matching compares the leading designator so decorations never block. The first flight that logs a ladder winner settles the gate.select contract — record it in docs/integrations/gsx-remote-api.md.

checks: Every gate.select refusal 'not_found' now has a gsx-gate-not-found event with the mirror's airport, parkings count, nearest names and an 8-name sample. READ IT: parkings = 0 means GSX sent no parking list for that airport (the dispatch sent too early or the mirror missed the patch); parkings > 0 with a sample like 'Gate W40' while the token 'W40' was refused means GSX's own suffix search did not match — quote both, that is the next design decision.

With gsx.answerPositionMenuWithArrivalGate true and GSX raising 'Select Position at <destination>' while a gate request stood: one gsx-gate-position-menu event per attempt (max 2) with outcome Success | NoRow | ItemNotAvailable | AmbiguousMatch | MenuTitleMismatch | GsxNoResponse, the facility row picked and the page rows. Success must be followed by gsx-gate-confirmed (readback) or the Assigned(unconfirmed) status after 60 s; GSX's anchored facility (the 'Change Facility [...]' row in the next parking-change menu) must then name the requested gate.
assert-absent: a menu.pick issued on a 'Select Position at' page whose picked row does not contain the requested token or a range covering it (the planner must never guess).

In-flight airport pick (#141 symptom): gsx-gate-airport-pick with outcome GsxNoResponse 'menu did not appear' means GSX showed no menu in flight; report whether the pilot had opened the GSX toolbar menu once after takeoff (the manual's workaround) — if yes and it still failed, #141 is not the whole story. From the #141 fix on (2026-10-05) the detail reads 'menu did not appear (menu.open acknowledged but nothing appeared; the menu LVAR showed nothing either)' only when BOTH rungs failed — a pick that went through after 'requested through the menu LVAR' is the fix working.
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-04 (#156). EGLL→EFHK 2026-10-03 rc.8: airport pick ×3 'menu did not appear', gate.select 'W40' ×4 not_found with EFHK loaded, GSX parked the aircraft at Stand 401 and asked Select Position itself. The position-menu answer is off by default and unverified live; its menu shape (facility groups with '(Gates W34-W48)' ranges → 'All … positions' page) is from that flight's log.

checks: When an arrival gate was armed and GSX had the destination loaded: a gsx-gate-resolved event BEFORE the first gate.select of that dispatch, carrying the scenery identity (e.g. 'Gate W40'), GSX's name ('Apron 1W (Gates W34-W48) | Gate 40'), the confidence and the token list starting with the integer number. The first gate.select command in the log must then carry that integer ({"gate":40}), and succeed (ok|prepared|already_selected) or be followed by the next rung — never by the bare typed token first.

Log line 'Parking catalogue for <ICAO>: N stands from <notes>' names which tiers answered (gsx-profile: <files>; facility: N parkings, M jetways). facility missing on a flight with MSFS connected = the facility definition failed — look for 'Facility definition failed' or a SimConnect exception DATA_ERROR/INVALID_DATA_TYPE/INVALID_DATA_SIZE near connect; quote the field list in FacilityDefinition.Fields for the fix.

Log line 'Parking positions at <ICAO>: N stands known to two sources, median offset X m' — X under ~30 m confirms the facility BIAS_X/BIAS_Z east/north convention; 'LARGE' means an axis is flipped (fix AirportFacilityService.Offset, then re-verify).
On the OFP page (requires-human): typing the gate shows the 'GSX knows it as …' line within a second; after Confirm the 'Stand:' line repeats it.

assert-absent: gsx-gate-not-found for a stand that a gsx-gate-resolved event named with confidence Exact — GSX refused the number of a stand the scenery has: quote both events and the mirror parkings count.
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-04 (Option A + B, unverified live). Root cause of the four 'W40' refusals: the EFHK .py template '… | Gate #§' drops the GATE letter, so GSX's name is 'Gate 40'. The resolver sends the parking NUMBER first. See docs/integrations/gsx-profiles.md.

checks: While parked at the departure stand with an OFP (or FMS) runway: a pushback-suggestion event with the stand, runway, options (label, kind, heading, headingSource) and the suggestion + confidence + reason. headingSource 'profile' = the GSX ini release position; 'label' = compass word; 'geometry' = ±90° from the stand heading. REPORT whether the suggested direction was the one the pilot actually wanted (ATC's clearance) — that is the only real verdict for the advisor.

When GSX raised 'Select pushback direction': exactly one pushback-direction-decision event per menu appearance with kind Pick|Ask|Leave, the reason and the menu lines. Pick must be followed by the executor's 'pushback direction selection' success in the log and GSX pushing that way; Ask must be followed by a pushback-question event (prompt + options) and, if the pilot answered, a pushback-choice event and then a second decision with kind Pick ('pilot chose …'); an unanswered question ends with pushback-question {outcome: unanswered} and the menu left open.

Voice: 'push back facing <compass>' / 'tail left' / 'tail right' produce pushback-choice with source voice and a readback naming the matched line ('that is tail right here') or the refusal ('no route faces …'). The Korry buttons on the OFP page produce source web.
assert-absent: two pushback-direction-decision events with kind Pick in the same GSX session (the once-per-session latch), and any Pick whose entry is not one of the event's own entries.

requires-human: the FO question 'Pushback — tail left or tail right?' (or the stand's custom labels) is heard once, not repeated; the Korry buttons on the OFP page light the pilot's choice (or the confident suggestion) and the 'Suggested: …' line reads sensibly for the stand and runway.
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-04 (owner Option 1, all five suggestions incl. voice; unverified live). Default mode changed to auto — users with an explicit pushbackPreference 'straight'/'tailLeft'/'tailRight' in settings.json keep the old fixed behaviour. Advisor rules in docs/integrations/gsx-profiles.md §7.

checks: When GSX does not recognize the parking (spawn at an unknown stand): a ground-prep hold with reason 'GSX has not identified the parking — select the stand in the GSX menu, or reposition' (visible on the Flight Status card; from the #141 fix on it is preceded by '… opening the GSX menu so it looks for the stand' and a 'gsx-parking-wake' {outcome: 'menu-without-parking'} — see probe gsx-parking-wake), AND an 'fo.parking-conflict-advisory' spoken event, once per conflict — including when the only GSX surface is the 'Select Position at ...' menu (the 2026-08-23 gap: only the parking-CHANGE menu was wired, so the hold stayed a log line).
assert-absent: repeated app restarts around a parking-change menu with session gate 'unknown' and no pilot-facing guidance (the 2026-08-17/22 signature).
A 'gsx-question' decision 'position-select menu ... left for the user' when the Select Position menu appears (no more anonymous 'no question handler').
probes.notes: Re-fixed 2026-08-23: the unknown-parking HOLD itself now publishes the parking conflict (advisory + status row), so no particular menu shape is required; the Select Position menu is a named catalogue decision. The app still never clicks GSX's parking menus — it advises. 2026-09-21: the Select Position menu is a conflict ONLY when GSX raised it (not our reposition) at a parked, engines-off aircraft — see probe parking-advisory-false-alarm.

checks: assert-absent: an 'fo.parking-conflict-advisory' event within 60 s after a 'gsx-decision' reposition ('repositioning at <gate>') whose position pick succeeded — the 2026-09-13 EGLL 546 and 2026-09-20 LIRF 835 signature: our own Reposition Aircraft → Select Position submenu was taken for GSX's unknown-parking prompt and the FO said 'GSX doesn't recognise our parking position' at a stand GSX had armed 90 s earlier.
assert-present: when the reposition runs, the 'gsx-question' decision for the position-select menu reads 'opened by our own reposition step — GSX knows the stand; not a parking conflict'.

assert-absent: an 'fo.parking-conflict-advisory' event while the phase is TakeoffRoll..TaxiIn or while any engine is running (2026-09-20 EGLL: spoken 31 s after touchdown on the landing roll). A conflict published while moving records 'fo.parking-conflict-held' instead and speaks only if it still stands once parked with engines off.

assert-present: when GSX names the parking after a conflict stood (mirror 'parking'/'handlerData' update with a gate key), the log line 'GSX identified the parking <gate> — parking conflict cleared' (2026-09-20: the Select Position conflict outlived the pilot's stand pick by the whole deboarding).

assert-absent (#157): an 'fo.parking-conflict-advisory' (or 'fo.parking-conflict-held') on an arrival where a 'gsx-gate-assigned' stands and the 'Change parking or service' menu names that gate ('Change Facility [<the gate GSX answered in the gsx-gate-assigned payload>]'). The 2026-10-04 LKPR signature: gate.select 29 → 'Gate C 29' at 21:34:52Z, menu 'Change Facility [Gate C 29]' at 21:36:29Z with the session gate unknown, FO 'GSX doesn't recognise our parking position' at 21:41:09Z, GSX identified Gate C 29 at 21:44:06Z and deboarded.

assert-present (#157): in that case the 'gsx-question' decision for the parking-change menu reads '... the arrival gate <gate> it accepted; not a parking conflict'. A facility that names ANOTHER stand must still publish the conflict.

assert-absent (#157): an 'fo.parking-conflict-advisory' less than 20 s after the first 'ground prep' decision 'holding: GSX has not identified the parking' of that hold (2026-10-04 EFHK: spoken at 18:52:24Z, GSX named Gate 35 7.5 s later). A hold that ends inside the 20 s publishes nothing.

assert-absent (#141): the line 'GSX doesn't recognise our parking position' at a stand GSX names as soon as its menu is opened (2026-10-05 LKPR rc.17: FO at 01:04:38Z, the pilot's toolbar click at 01:04:49Z, 'Gate C 28' at 01:04:50Z). The prep hold now opens the menu itself — probe gsx-parking-wake.
probes.notes: Fixed 2026-09-21 (0.4.0-rc.3): GsxMenuIntentExecutor.IsDriving (intent chain + 5 s grace) gates the Select Position handler; ParkingConflictGate.IsParkedEnginesOff gates both the catalogue publish and the FO advisory (held while moving, re-checked on the at-gate phase edge); GsxBootstrapService clears the conflict when the mirror names a parking. 2026-10-05 (#157): the parking-change menu is not a conflict when its facility is the assigned arrival gate (GsxGateResolver.FacilityNamesGate, whole-word compare against the gate.select payload name, else the typed token); the departure prep hold publishes the conflict only after GsxGroundPrepCoordinator.UnknownParkingGrace (20 s).

checks: Trigger = a 'ground prep' decision 'holding: GSX has not identified the parking — opening the GSX menu so it looks for the stand' (GSX Ready, in session, at the gate, no '/parking' in the mirror — the pilot must NOT have opened the GSX menu before starting ground services). Behaviour = a 'gsx-parking-wake' event {outcome: 'opening'} on the next prep cycle (3–10 s into the hold), then {outcome: 'named'} with the stand ('GSX named the parking <gate> (menu.open; menu closed)' or '… opened through the menu LVAR …'), then 'Ground preparation hold released' and 'Ground prep -> Reposition' within two prep cycles — all without a pilot click. The 2026-10-05 LKPR rc.17 signature it replaces: hold 01:04:13Z, FO 'GSX doesn't recognise our parking position' 01:04:38Z, pilot's toolbar click 01:04:49Z, '/parking' 'Gate C 28' 01:04:50Z.
assert-absent: an 'fo.parking-conflict-advisory' between the hold and a 'gsx-parking-wake' {outcome: 'named'} — a parking GSX names once its menu is asked for was never a conflict.

Report WHICH rung worked: detail '(menu.open…' = the Remote API woke GSX on a fresh session; '…opened through the menu LVAR…' = menu.open was acknowledged with no menu (the #141 signature) and L:FSDT_GSX_MENU_OPEN did it. Either is a pass; the split settles #141's hypothesis. With the wire trace on, quote the '/state' patch (3 'taxing on ground' → 5 'Parked') and the '/parking' patch that follow the request.
assert-present: after {outcome: 'named'} the root menu is not left on screen — a 'menu.close' command follows when the shown menu is 'Activate Services at …' (the reposition step re-opens it itself).

When {outcome: 'menu-without-parking'}: the menu named in the detail stays up, nothing is picked, and the conflict guidance is the old line ('… Select the stand in the GSX menu, or reposition the aircraft.') — the genuine #44 case.

When {outcome: 'menu-unreachable'} (no rung showed a menu): the hold reason reads '… its menu did not open — open the GSX menu once from the toolbar' and the FO line is 'Captain, GSX has not found our stand yet, and its menu won't open for me. Open the GSX menu once from the toolbar, and I'll take it from there.' — at most 3 attempts per hold, 30 s apart; a later attempt that works clears the conflict.
assert-absent: a 'gsx-parking-wake' {outcome: 'opening'} while a GSX menu is already shown, while any engine runs, or while the aircraft moves.

In flight (#141's first sighting): an in-flight airport pick whose menu.open shows nothing now logs 'GSX menu: menu.open acknowledged but nothing appeared — requested through the menu LVAR'; report whether the pick then succeeded.
probes.notes: Built 2026-10-05 (0.6.0-rc.18). First live pass the same day, LKPR Gate C 28, new MSFS session, pilot did not touch the GSX menu: hold 01:29:28Z, 'opening' 01:29:33.860Z, menu.open ok 01:29:33.876Z, 'GSX named the parking Gate C 28 (menu.open; menu closed)' 01:29:36.391Z, hold released 01:29:38Z, prep complete 01:30:18Z, no FO advisory — the Remote API rung alone woke GSX. Root cause from the rc.17 wire trace: GSX evaluates the parking only when its menu is requested; the prep chain waited for a parking name before any step that opens the menu. GsxParkingWakeService (pure ParkingWakePlan) runs from the unknown-parking hold of GsxGroundPrepCoordinator; GsxMenuOpener (menu.open, then L:FSDT_GSX_MENU_OPEN = 1) is shared with GsxMenuIntentExecutor and the web menu card. The conflict is published only when the wake is Unresolved or MenuUnreachable AND the 20 s grace has run (GsxGroundPrepCoordinator.ConflictDue). Still unknown: whether the LVAR rung opens the menu when menu.open shows nothing (never exercised yet), and the in-flight airport pick.

checks: When an arrival gate is armed and the phase reaches Cruise (or Descent/Approach) with GSX still reporting the departure airport: a 'gsx-gate-airport-pick' session event (payload destination, outcome, detail, attempt, entries) and the log line 'Gate request <gate>: Armed — loading <ICAO> in GSX (in-flight airport pick, attempt N)'. REPORT the page title and rows quoted in the 'In-flight airport pick ... not completed' line on failure — that is how we learn GSX's in-flight menu shape. SETTLED 2026-10-04 (EFHK→LKPR, #157): in flight the GSX ROOT page is itself titled 'Select airport' and its rows carry the ICAO ('LKPR Ruzyne at 592.70 nm [PLANNED]') — there is no root entry to pick first. From the #157 fix on, outcome 'ItemNotAvailable' with detail 'no entry matches ^select airport on 'Select airport'' is a FAILURE (the pre-fix result: ItemNotAvailable at 20:03:09Z, 21:08:23Z and 21:31:44Z on that flight); expect 'Intent in-flight airport pick succeeded: picked '<ICAO> …''.

On success: 'GSX loaded <ICAO> from the in-flight airport pick', then 'GSX command gate.select {"gate":"<as typed>"...} -> ok (prepared|ok)' IN THE AIR, then 'gsx-gate-assigned' and, within 60 s, 'gsx-gate-confirmed' from the SetGate LVAR readback. After landing NO 'Select Position at <destination>' menu and no parking conflict — services engage on arrival.

assert-absent: a gate.select sent while parked (on ground, stopped, engines off). The planner must record 'gsx-gate-too-late' + 'too late — GSX already has the aircraft parked at a stand' instead of a send (the 2026-08-22 EGLL 313 and 2026-09-13 LIRF 829 signature).
If the name send is refused not_found and a unique parking number exists: 'gsx-gate-number-fallback' + a second gate.select with "gate":<integer>. REPORT whether the integer was accepted.
assert-absent: more than one airport-pick attempt within 2 minutes, or more than 12 in a flight.
probes.notes: Added 2026-09-21 (0.4.0-rc.4) from the GSX Pro integration guide §8.14 + Handler Scripts guide selectGate: gate.select refuses while parked (surfaces as not_found), the token as typed resolves by suffix, and GSX only loads the destination in flight if picked from its 'Select airport' menu. First flight verifies the in-flight menu shape; the pick fails soft (menu closed again) and the ground taxi-in send still runs. 2026-10-05 (#157): the executor runs the row pick directly when the page it opened is already 'Select airport' (GsxMenuIntentExecutor: a parent whose open lands on the child's page picks nothing; the title must hold for 300 ms after our own menu.open). The first ok gate.select ever was 2026-10-04 21:34:52Z, integer token 29, airborne (the three airport picks before it had failed; how GSX came to have LKPR loaded is not established — read the wire trace).

checks: When any gate.select is refused: a 'GSX command gate.select failure detail: error={...} payload={...}' log line right after the 'GSX command gate.select ... -> failed (not_found)' summary. REPORT the error object verbatim — it is the only evidence we have for what GSX matches the gate token against (every shape tried 2026-08-09 → 2026-09-20 was refused: ' Gate D27', 'D27', 'D5', 'Stand 313', '313', 'Stand 546', 'Terminal 5B (531-548)|Stand 546', '546', 'Stand 829', 'Stand 835', 'Remote Stands 8XX/9XX | Stand 835', '835').

When a gate.select succeeds: a 'GSX command gate.select result payload: {...}' line — record the accepted token shape in docs/integrations/gsx-remote-api.md §6 and flip this probe to closed-regression-watch.
probes.notes: Added 2026-09-21 (0.4.0-rc.3). gate.select has never returned ok in any recorded flight; the client used to log only the result code. Also turn on logging.wireTrace for the next flight so the full frames are available. SETTLED 2026-10-04 (EFHK→LKPR, ticket t-20261004-2147): the first ok — 'gate.select {"gate":29}' (the parking NUMBER as an integer, sent airborne) answered ok/prepared with uiName 'Gate C 29'.
