checks: When the flight reached Cruise: at least one 'flight-progress' event with fractionBasis 'Position' AND etaBasis 'Position', carrying lat/lon, routeNm, flownNm, toGoNm and fraction. flownNm + toGoNm must be >= routeNm (triangle inequality; equal only on the direct line) and fraction must rise over the flight.

An 'airport-coordinates' event after the OFP fetch with origin.found and destination.found true — REPORT each 'source' (gateway or dfd) and the log line 'Gateway airport <ICAO>: N runway(s), M coordinate point(s) -> …': which reading of the gateway's lat/lng pair applied is the open empirical question (docs/integrations/prosim.md §2). Compare the reported lat/lon with the real airport reference point; more than ~3 nm off is a wire-shape bug.
Sanity: routeNm for the leg matches the known great-circle distance within 1 % (EGLL–LIRF ≈ 780 nm, EGLL–EKCH ≈ 529 nm, EGLL–EHAM ≈ 200 nm).

'flight-sample' events carry lat/lon in the air (4 decimals) and the values move; on the ground at the stand they hold still and unchanged samples stay suppressed (no one-per-second flood while parked).
assert-absent: lat 0 / lon 0 on any 'flight-sample' or 'flight-progress' event — exactly (0, 0) must be dropped as 'no position'.

A 'Flight progress: fraction Time … ETA Time' log line in mid-flight means position or airport coordinates were lost — report the 'position' / 'origin' / 'destination' fields on that line. Before off-blocks and with no OFP it is expected.

CALIBRATION (report, no verdict): list vnavDistanceRemainingRaw and fmsTimeToDestSecRaw beside toGoNm / etaUtc on each 'flight-progress' event. If vnavDistanceRemainingRaw tracks toGoNm (a little larger, shrinking at ground speed) it is an along-route distance to the destination in nm and should replace the direct distance in the T/D estimate.
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-03 (October batch package 1). Events: 'airport-coordinates' (once per OFP, on resolve), 'flight-progress' (on every basis change and every 5 min while airborne), 'tod-approaching' (see tod-approaching-once). Distances are great-circle DIRECT by design — toGoNm under-reads the route distance; that is not a failure.

checks: assert-absent: two 'tod-approaching' events for the same destination within one flight — the moment is once per flight (it re-arms only on the ground before the next departure, or on a flight-cycle reset).

assert-present when the flight cruised with flightStatus.todLeadMinutes > 0: exactly one 'tod-approaching' event, with minutesToTod <= leadMinutes, estimate true, and cruiseAltitudeFt / destinationElevationFt / descentDistanceNm consistent with (cruise − elevation) / 1000 × 3.

TIMING (report, no verdict): the gap between the 'tod-approaching' timestamp and the 'phase-changed' commit into Descent. The 3:1 estimate on a direct distance errs EARLY, so the gap should be leadMinutes or more; a gap much SHORTER than leadMinutes (the descent began before the estimate said so) is worth an issue comment with cruiseAltitudeFt, distanceToGoNm and groundSpeedKt quoted.
An app restart or ProSim reconnect inside the lead window must NOT produce a second event (no crossing was seen); a restart outside it must still produce the one event.
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-03 (October batch package 1). No speech hangs off this event yet — package 4 (FO monitoring) and package 7 (notifications) consume it. destinationElevationFt null = the airport source had no elevation and sea level was assumed.

checks: When the flight landed (a 'phase-changed' commit into LandingRollout): one 'touchdown' event 5–8 s later carrying verticalSpeedFpm, iasKt, groundSpeedKt, pitchDeg, bankDeg, bounces, wentAround and outcome (landed / went-around), with the matching log line 'Touchdown: <n> fpm, IAS … GS … pitch … bank …, <n> bounce(s)'.

verticalSpeedFpm is NEGATIVE and plausible (−30 to −700 for a normal landing). Cross-check with the 'flight-sample' events around contactUtc: the event's rate must be at least as negative as the 'vs' of the last airborne samples and more negative than the first on-ground sample — the recorder takes the most negative value of the last second, not the sample at contact.
groundSpeedKt agrees with the LandingRollout 'phase-changed' snapshot.groundSpeedKt within a few knots (the phase commit trails contact by the engine's debounce).
REPORT pitchDeg with its sign: a normal landing is 3–7° nose-up. A NEGATIVE value settles that aircraft.pitch is nose-up-negative and the sign must be flipped (docs/integrations/prosim.md).

CALIBRATION (report, no verdict): quote accelerationYRawBeforeContact, accelerationYRawMax and accelerationYRawMin. The pre-contact baseline names the unit — about 1 = G with gravity, about 0 = G without, about 9.8 = m/s², about 32 = ft/s². Nothing may show or convert these until the owner confirms.

After shutdown: a 'logbook.folded' event whose touchdownVerticalSpeedFpm equals the 'touchdown' event's verticalSpeedFpm, and the debrief text ('speech.spoken' / the .debrief.txt file) contains 'Touchdown at minus <rate rounded to 10> feet per minute'.
'flight-times' events carry offBlocksUtc → takeoffUtc → landingUtc → onBlocksUtc filling in order, each stamp never changing once set.
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-03 (October batch package 2). The event is written only once the landing has settled (ground contact held 5 s), so it is absent if the app or the sim session ended inside those 5 s. A touchdown needs 5 s airborne first — a rejected takeoff produces none.

checks: assert-absent: two 'touchdown' events within 10 s — one landing is one event; the bounce count rides on it instead of producing a second one.
A bounced landing (the pilot will say so) shows bounces >= 1 on ONE event. A raw on-ground flicker with no real bounce must show bounces 0.

A touch-and-go or a go-around after touchdown: one event with wentAround true (written about 5 s after the wheels left the ground), then a second event with wentAround false for the landing that ended the flight. The logbook flight and the debrief use the second.
assert-absent: a 'touchdown' event while the phase is TakeoffRoll, TaxiOut or any at-gate phase with no airborne phase before it in the session.
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-03 (October batch package 2). Bounces are edges of the COMMITTED ground contact (flightState.groundContactAgreeSamples at the engine's 250 ms tick), so a bounce shorter than about half a second is not counted — by design.

checks: When a briefing or the debrief was spoken with the LLM on and briefing.streamLlm on: one 'llm.stream' event per narration carrying kind, firstTokenMs, firstAudioMs, sentencesSpoken, templateTookOver, takeoverReason, sectionsFromTemplate, preempted, outcome and model. REPORT firstTokenMs and firstAudioMs — the numbers the feature is judged by (expected: first audio a few seconds after the request instead of after the whole reply).

'speech.segment' events follow for each sentence (reason 'llm' for the model's own sentences, none for template ones), all between ONE 'speech.dequeued' and ONE 'speech.spoken' for the item (text 'Departure briefing' / 'Arrival briefing' / 'Post-flight debrief', reason 'stream — N segment(s)').

When templateTookOver is true: REPORT takeoverReason and the log line before it — 'a streamed sentence failed number verification (unverified: …)' names the number the model got wrong; 'stalled', 'timed out', 'the LLM stream failed' name the other causes. A takeover is the rule WORKING, not a failure; a takeover on every briefing means the model or the prompt needs work.

assert-absent: a 'speech.segment' whose text holds a number that is not one of the briefing's facts (cross-check against the OFP, the METAR and the FMS values of the flight: runway heading, transition altitude, V-speeds, wind, QNH, ILS frequency, minima). Spelled-out numbers count — 'one six eight' is 168.

The segments spoken after a verify-failed takeover are template sentences in template order ('Initial track 163 degrees.', 'Wind 250 at 14 knots.', 'QNH 1013.' …) and never repeat a section whose numbers the model had already spoken.
'briefing.spoken' / 'debrief.spoken' with streamed true carry the text that was actually heard (the model's sentences plus any template sections), not the model's full reply.
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-03 (October batch package 3; owner decisions D1-A, D2-1, D3-1, D4-1 on the issue). The debrief's llm.stream event has kind 'debrief'. With briefing.streamLlm off none of these events exist and the whole-reply path's 'debrief.styled' / 'briefing.spoken' (no streamed flag) apply.

checks: assert-absent: a 'speech.requeued' event for a streamed item (text exactly 'Departure briefing', 'Arrival briefing' or 'Post-flight debrief') — a streamed narration cut by a Critical ENDS (speech.preempted then speech.dropped 'pre-empted', llm.stream preempted true, outcome Superseded); it must never be put back to restart from the top. The whole-reply path's restart of a Normal item (text = the full narrative) is unchanged and still allowed.
assert-absent: any 'speech.segment' of that item after its 'speech.preempted'.

When a High callout ('callout.fired' / tag callout) was enqueued while a stream was speaking: its 'speech.dequeued' reason reads 'between stream segments' and it was spoken between two 'speech.segment' events — not after the item's 'speech.spoken'.
assert-absent: a Normal or Low 'speech.spoken' between two 'speech.segment' events of one stream (nothing at the stream's priority or below may interleave).
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-03 (October batch package 3). Covers owner decisions D2 (a pre-empted stream ends) and D3 (High plays between sentences).

checks: Only when sop.monitoring.fuelCheck.enabled was true (the settings snapshot in the bundle, or the describer's disabled reason absent from the Voice Reference drawer): in a cruise longer than intervalMinutes, 'fuel.check' events with trigger 'periodic' and spoken true, spaced intervalMinutes apart (± one tick), the first one intervalMinutes AFTER the Cruise commit — never at cruise entry.

Each spoken event carries method 'navlog' when the OFP had a navlog and a position was known, else 'fallback'. With 'navlog': fix is a waypoint of the flight plan the aircraft has actually passed (compare the lat/lon of the nearest 'flight-sample' with the plan), fobKg within 50 kg of the FOB on that sample, plannedFobKg between the two neighbouring fixes' planned figures, differenceKg = fobKg − plannedFobKg, estimatedLandingKg = plannedLandingKg + differenceKg.

priority is 'high' only when shortfall is true (differenceKg <= −shortfallMarginKg); otherwise 'normal'. text matches the figures: tonnes to one decimal, difference rounded to 100 kilos or spoken as tonnes above 999.

A 'fuel.check' with trigger 'voice' follows every 'fuel check' / 'check the fuel' utterance ('speech.heard' or the intent event) — spoken false with reason 'no plan or no fuel figure' is legitimate only when no OFP was loaded.
assert-absent: 'fuel.check' with trigger 'periodic' outside the Cruise phase, or while flight-live was false, or with sop.monitoring.fuelCheck.enabled false.
DEBRIEF: the debrief after the flight now has fuel figures to quote (fobKg is what DebriefFactExtractor reads) — report whether the spoken debrief mentions fuel.
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-03 (October batch package 4). Off by default. 'Last fix passed' = the leg the aircraft is on (within 30 nm of it), else the nearest fix behind; on a direct routing the fix named may be the one the direct skipped — that is expected, not a bug. TOC/TOD are spoken as 'top of climb/descent'.

checks: With an OFP navlog loaded and a takeoff time: one fuel.log.fix per navlog fix passed, in index order, none before the takeoff (the origin row carries the takeoff time as atUtc). Cross-check against the flight-sample positions: a fix's atUtc must lie within ~2 minutes of the sample where the aircraft was nearest / abeam that fix.
fobKg on each row equals the FOB in the flight-sample nearest atUtc (±50 kg); deltaKg = fobKg − plannedFobKg.
Several rows with the same atUtc are allowed only after a gap in the samples (reconnect, long pause) — report them.

assert-absent (clock, fixed 2026-10-05): a fuel.log.fix whose atUtc is on a different clock from its plannedAtUtc. Signature = |deltaMinutes| of hundreds on every row after the origin, equal to the sim-to-real clock offset (the event's own 'timestamp' is the real clock; the flight-times event's takeoffUtc is the sim clock). On a flight flown with sim time ≠ real time every row's atUtc must follow takeoffUtc, not 'timestamp', and deltaMinutes must be a few minutes.

Consistency with the FO: a fuel.check event (navlog method) between two fixes reports plannedFobKg between those rows' plan figures and a differenceKg of the same sign and order as the neighbouring rows' deltaKg.
assert-absent: fuel.log.fix after a new OFP was fetched with the OLD route's fix names; the log must restart (rows for the new plan only).
The destination row stamps when the aircraft reaches the end of the final leg (fraction ≥ 0.99), i.e. around touchdown — not at the gate after taxi-in and not never.
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-04 (#154, Fuel Log tab). FuelLogService ticks every 5 s in Core — runs with the voice FO off. The page's 'Fuel check now' button records a fuel.check with trigger 'page'. 2026-10-05 (0.6.0-rc.15, EFHK departure, sim 03:54Z / real 19:44Z): fixes were stamped with the PC clock against a sim-clock takeoff — deltaMinutes 948 on every row; FuelLogService and FuelCheckMonitor (check time, ETA fallback) now read ISimClock.UtcNowOrReal.

checks: Only when sop.monitoring.grossErrorCheck.enabled was true: exactly one 'fo.gross-error-check' with trigger 'automatic' per final loadsheet edition, AFTER the 'loadsheet' final Sent event and after the FMS PERF TO page had V1/VR/V2 (the datarefs aircraft.fms.perf.takeOff.v1/vr/v2 > 0) — never before the final was sent, never twice for the same edition, and never in the air.

result 'checked' when the live ZFW was within zfwToleranceKg of the final loadsheet ZFW, FOB within blockFuelToleranceKg of the block fuel, and the FMS flaps/flex/V-speeds within tolerance of the Takeoff performance page result; result 'mismatch' lists each difference in 'mismatches' and the spoken text names them. skipped names what could not be compared ('takeoff performance' when the Takeoff page was never used this flight — report, not a failure).
A revised final (new EditionNumber) produces a second event; a flight-cycle reset or a turnaround back at the gate re-arms it.
A 'gross error check' utterance produces an event with trigger 'voice' at any phase while flight-live, even with Automatic off.
assert-absent (machine): two 'fo.gross-error-check' events with the same trigger inside 10 minutes — the once-per-edition rule failed.
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-03 (October batch package 4). Off by default. The FMS INIT B ZFW/block entries are write-only in the ProSim SDK (aircraft.fms.init.* CanRead false), so the aircraft's own aircraft.weight.zfw and total fuel stand in for 'what the FMS was given' — a wrong INIT B entry shows as a wrong GW/V-speeds, which the V-speed comparison catches.

checks: Only when sop.monitoring.destinationWeather.enabled was true and the destination weather actually changed between hero-weather refreshes in Cruise/Descent/Approach: an 'fo.destination-weather' event per change with icao = the OFP destination, triggers ⊆ [visibility, ceiling, atis, tailwind], text matching the trigger ('Destination visibility now … below …', 'Destination ceiling …', 'Destination ATIS now information <letter>', 'Wind at destination ddd at nn knots: a n knot tailwind on runway …').

Compare the 'metar' field of consecutive events: each event must correspond to a real change in the raw METAR (visibility group, cloud group, ATIS letter, wind group) — an event with an identical METAR to the previous one is a false edge.
belowThreshold true ⇒ the text ends with an 'Alternate <name>: …' line when the alternate card had an observation; false ⇒ no alternate line.
Rate limit: no two events sharing a trigger inside minutesBetweenAnnouncements (default 15). Different triggers may follow each other sooner.

assert-absent: an event at the first observation of the flight unless the destination was already below a limit then (baseline rule); any event before Cruise; any event after a destination change describing the OLD destination.
If no event fired all flight (weather stable, or disabled) the probe is 'no evidence', not a failure — note it.
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-03 (October batch package 4). Off by default. Rides the hero weather store's refresh cadence; the planned landing runway comes from the OFP (plan_rwy) and its heading is the designator × 10 (magnetic) against the METAR's true wind — a few degrees of variation are inside the threshold's purpose.

checks: Only when sop.monitoring.readbacks.enabled was true: an 'fo.readback' event per read-back utterance ('altimeter one zero one three', 'V speeds …', 'runway two seven right', 'minimums …'), kind ∈ altimeter|vspeeds|runway|minimums, said = the figures heard, outcome ∈ checked|mismatch|unavailable|incomplete, and text = what the FO answered.

outcome 'checked' only when the aircraft agreed: compare said with the EFIS baro dataref (altimeter, ± altimeterToleranceHpa), the FMS PERF TO V-speeds (± vSpeedToleranceKt each), the departure runway the briefing resolved (phases before TakeoffRoll) or the arrival runway (after), and the briefed minima (± minimumsToleranceFt). A 'mismatch' text must quote the aircraft's actual value.
'minimums check' and 'altimeter check' (bare lead-ins, no figure) must NOT produce an 'fo.readback' event — those phrases belong to the checklist / callout features and must still work.
No 'fo.readback' while flight-live was false — the FO answers 'No flight data to check that against.' instead ('speech.spoken' with that text).

GRAMMAR: with the closed recognizer, the lead-ins must appear in the grammar snapshot ('speech.grammar' / the Voice Reference drawer under Read-backs with the value badge) — report if a read-back was transcribed but not routed (an 'intent' miss event right after a read-back-shaped 'speech.heard').
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-03 (October batch package 4). Off by default. StandaloneReadbacks is registered BEFORE the Radio and FCU executors so 'altimeter …' / 'runway …' are not swallowed as settings commands; it declines any utterance without a figure so the existing bare phrases keep their owners.

checks: Only when speech.foQuestions.enabled was true and the LAN ASR was the active engine: every free-form question the pilot asked ('speech.heard' / the ASR decision trail line 'ASR heard "…" -> Reject') is followed by one 'fo.query' and one 'fo.answer' with the same question text; outcome ∈ answered | answered-on-retry | unverified | timed-out | sterile | llm-offline | busy | preempted.

For outcome 'answered' or 'answered-on-retry': every number in 'text' (digits or spelled) appears in the fact sheet the app had at the time — cross-check against the telemetry snapshot nearest the event (FOB, GS, altitude, ETA, distances). A wrong figure spoken as 'answered' is the one failure that matters: quote question, text and the live value.

A question whose answer is NOT in the facts ('what is the captain's name') must come back as "I don't have that." (outcome answered — the model said the fixed phrase) or 'unverified' — never an invented figure.

TIMING (report): firstTokenMs / firstAudioMs / totalMs per answer. totalMs > 6000 with outcome 'timed-out' means the model is too slow for the default budget — report the model name. A 'Stand by.' 'speech.spoken' between the question and the answer is expected when firstAudioMs > 2000.

assert-absent: any 'fo.query' while flight-live phases were TakeoffRoll / InitialClimb / LandingRollout or below the sterile ceiling in Climb/Descent/Approach that produced a 'speech.spoken' — the only allowed record there is outcome 'sterile' with no speech.

assert-absent: an exact feature phrase ('request refueling', 'fuel check', 'altimeter …') producing an 'fo.query' — known phrases must win. An 'fo.answer' text containing a command phrase must NOT be followed by that feature's event (no 'gsx.*', no FCU/radio write log line within 5 s) — the read-only rule.
assert-absent: 'fo.query' while the recognizer engine was systemSpeech (the 'Recognition … (systemSpeech)' log line is the engine marker) — questions are LAN-engine only.

SMALL TALK (#152, only when speech.foQuestions.smallTalk was true): every fo.query / fo.answer carries mode flight | chat | chat→flight. A question containing a flight word (fuel, weight, speed, altitude, runway, weather, time, passengers, descent, gate…) must be mode flight; one without must be mode chat. A chat answer may contain figures, but assert-absent: a chat answer whose text contains a flight-data word (fuel, tonnes, kilos, feet, knots, flight level, heading, runway, QNH, altitude, passengers, zulu, ETA, descent, weight, nautical) together with a figure — the guard must have refused it (outcome unverified). A chat answer that is exactly "Let me check." (mode chat→flight) must be followed by a mode-flight fo.answer for the same question.
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-03 (October batch package 5). Off by default. Sterile cockpit drops the question without a word by owner decision (a 'stand by, after ten thousand' would itself be the chatter the SOP forbids). The strict re-ask happens only when verification failed BEFORE any speech; a half-spoken answer that then fails ends with the fixed line and no re-ask. 'busy' = a second question while one was being answered. 2026-10-03: small talk (#152) added — chat path = no fact sheet, no number verification, per-sentence flight-figure guard, "Let me check." hand-over to the strict path.

checks: Only when speech.foQuestions.whereAreWe was true: every place question ('what are we flying over', 'where are we', 'what is that city on the left', 'what country is this') produces one fo.query and one fo.answer with mode geo. A place question answered with mode flight ("I don't have that.") is the failure: quote it.

The fo.answer text begins with the atlas line ("We're over …" / "We're right over …" / "We're about … of …"), and the place it names agrees with the telemetry position nearest the event (lat/lon on the flight-sample): the named country contains the position, the reference town lies within ~120 nm in the stated compass direction (we are SOUTH-EAST of a town that bears north-west), and the stated distance matches within the spoken rounding (nearest mile under 10, 5 under 50, 10 above). A wrong country or a town on the wrong side is the one failure that matters.

factSource ∈ atlas | model | wikipedia. 'atlas' = the position line alone (model down, model refused by the guard, or nothing nearby); with speech.foQuestions.wikipediaFacts true and a reference town present, expect 'wikipedia' most of the time — a run of 'model' means the fetch fails (report; the debug log line 'Wikipedia summary for … failed' says why).

assert-absent: an fo.answer in mode geo whose fact sentences (everything after the first atlas sentences) contain a distance, bearing, position or coordinate, or a flight-data word (fuel, tonnes, feet, knots, flight level, heading, runway, QNH, altitude, passengers, zulu, ETA) together with a figure — the position comes only from the atlas and the chat guard must have refused such a sentence.
A place question with no position (fo.answer text = "I don't have our position right now.") is only correct while the flight-sample shows no lat/lon.

Sterile cockpit, busy, preempted: the same rules as fo-question-answer. The atlas line needs no LLM: with the LLM down the answer must still carry the position line with factSource atlas, never the llm-offline advisory.
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-04 (#153). Off by default; two switches (whereAreWe, wikipediaFacts). Position line is deterministic from the shipped atlas (Natural Earth 110m countries, 50m seas/regions, GeoNames towns >= 25k + capitals/seats); the side (left/right/ahead/behind) is relative to TRUE TRACK, not heading — in a strong crosswind a town 'ahead' may sit a few degrees off the nose. Regions wider than 40 square degrees (North European Plain, Siberia) are deliberately not named.

checks: When webUi.https.enabled was true: exactly one of the start-up log lines 'HTTPS listener up at https://…' or 'HTTPS listener: <problem>' — never both, never neither. 'Web UI available at http://…' must still appear in every case (HTTP never depends on HTTPS).
With a usable certificate: 'HTTPS listener up at https://<lan-ip>:<port>' and NO 'webUi.https' config-problem entry in the diagnostics bundle's problems list.

With a missing file, wrong password or a PFX without a private key: 'HTTPS listener: … — HTTP only.' AND the config-problem entry (area 'webUi.https'); the app started normally (modules started, web UI available).
With an expired certificate: 'HTTPS listener up at …' AND a 'webUi.https' problem whose text contains 'expired on' — both, by owner decision (ADR-0013 point 4).

assert-absent: a failed start ('terminated unexpectedly') with any HTTPS problem — HTTPS must never take HTTP down, including an HTTPS port already in use (that case logs 'already in use on this PC — HTTP only').
assert-absent: the PFX password, or any 'dpapi:' value, in any log line or diagnostics bundle.
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-03 (October batch package 6, ADR-0013). Off by default. The wake lock and the home-screen install are browser-side and have no server evidence beyond the install assets being fetched without the token (a 200 on /manifest.webmanifest from a non-loopback address with no cookie, if request logging is on) — they live on the human checklist.

checks: Only when notifications.enabled was true with at least one target: one 'notify.sent' per (milestone × target that wants it) — events ∈ refuel-complete | boarding-complete | final-loadsheet-sent | ready-for-pushback | cabin-secure | deice-holdover-expiring | top-of-descent-approaching | landed | on-blocks | deboarding-complete | test — each within a few seconds of its source evidence: the GSX 'Refueling' / 'Boarding' / 'Deboarding' Completed lifecycle events, 'gsx-departure-complete', 'cabin.secure' speech, 'tod-approaching', 'flight-times' (landing / on-blocks), the final 'loadsheet' Sent.

assert-absent: two 'notify.sent' for the same event AND target within one flight cycle (no 'gsx-flight-cycle-reset' between them) — EXCEPT final-loadsheet-sent, which may repeat with a higher edition.

'notify.failed' entries: report each reason (timeout | HTTP nnn | could not connect | cooldown | queue-full). A run of 'cooldown' drops right after one failure is the designed behaviour; 'queue-full' means the sender was wedged — quote the preceding failure.
ms on every 'notify.sent' must be under 5000 (the per-send timeout); a cluster near 5000 means the service is slow and the cooldown will start biting.

assert-absent: any target URL, token, 'Bearer ', ntfy topic path or Discord webhook path in the log or the session events — only 'target' (the user's name for it) and 'status' may appear. Also absent from the diagnostics bundle's settings copy (every 'url' and 'token' under notifications must read ***REDACTED***).

assert-absent: any ground-automation or speech stall that coincides with a slow send — the 'speech.spoken' and GSX decision cadence must not change around 'notify.*' timestamps (the dispatcher queues; it never awaits on a signal handler).
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-03 (October batch package 7). Off by default. Every milestone fires once per flight cycle from the Core signal source; the cabin-secure raise rides CabinCrewService's SecureReport, the refuel raise the GSX relay's Refueling Completed edge, ready-for-pushback the sequencer's all-done, TOD the flight-progress latch (#145). 'test' events come from the Send test button and may appear at any phase.

checks: The flight-times event at the takeoff edge carries takeoffFobKg; the one at touchdown landingFobKg; the one at shutdown onBlocksFobKg — each within ±100 kg of ProSim's fuel at that moment (the Fuel Log's origin row / fuel.check nearest in time are cross-checks).

The debrief's spoken fuel figures (speech.segment tag debrief / the .debrief.txt) equal, to one decimal tonne, the flight-times stamps: 'on blocks' = onBlocksFobKg (landingFobKg when the session ended before shutdown), 'used' = takeoffFobKg − that figure.

assert-absent: a debrief fuel figure that equals a mid-cruise fuel.check fobKg (to 0.1 t) while differing from the flight-times stamps — the 2026-10-04 EGLL→EFHK failure mode (first/last cruise check read as takeoff/landing).
A session with no fuel stamps (ProSim had no fuel figure at the edges) must produce a debrief with NO fuel sentence, never a figure from a fuel.check.
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-04 (#155). Before this, DebriefFactExtractor took the first and last fuel.check as start/final fuel — written when no fuel.check producer existed; #148's periodic cruise checks then fed it mid-cruise figures ('burned 1.7 t, landing with 5.1 t' on a 5 t flight).

checks: Trigger: ProSim connected (log 'Connected to ProSim'). Behaviour: one 'prosim-setup-check' session event per connection with prosimVersion and one items[] row per recommended IOS option (dataRef, label, recommended, actual, status in Ok|Mismatch|NotPresent|Ignored), plus the log line 'ProSim setup check (ProSim <version>): N ok, N to change, N not on this build, N ignored'.

Count the rows: 5 with the GSX pillar and door automation on (system.config.Config.DOORS, .GROUNDPOWER, Datalink.loadCargo, Datalink.loadFuel, Config.refuelRate); 2 (the two Datalink rows) with GSX off. On ProSim 1.75.1 no row may read NotPresent — every name exists there (verified 2026-10-06); a NotPresent row on another build is information, not a failure.

assert-absent: any gateway write to a system.config.* dataref (log 'ProSim setup: ... written') WITHOUT a 'prosim-setup-apply' session event in the same minute — a write that was not the pilot's click.

When a 'prosim-setup-apply' event exists: every name in attempted[] with a status that was Mismatch is in written[] or failed[]; the next 'prosim-setup-check' (the read-back) shows the written[] rows as Ok. A 'ProSim did not accept' note with the row still Mismatch is a failure to report with the dataref name.

Native guard, same connection: the GSX decision 'native GSX guard' reads either 'disabled 6 ProSim efb.gsx.* auto flags' (older ProSim) or 'this ProSim build has no efb.gsx.* flags — nothing to disable' (1.75.1). The old wording on 1.75.1 means the gateway verdict regressed (writeBool:false ignored).
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-06 (owner request). The IOS options are system.config.* datarefs, read and written through the port-5000 gateway without a restart (Door logic flipped true and back live on 1.75.1). Recommended values = the owner's working config. The check only reads; 'Apply recommended' on the Setup page is the only write. Unverified live in the app itself: the connection-time read, the card, the Apply click (the gateway calls were verified by hand).

checks: Trigger: an 'arrival-gate-confirmed' session event (payload gate, phase, origin pilot|atc) in ANY session of the flight, or an 'arrival-gate-restored' event in a later session of the same flight. Behaviour: before the flight-times touchdown stamp (the 'flight-times' event carrying landingFobKg, or the phase-changed edge into LandingRollout) the log holds at least one 'GSX command gate.select {...}' line for that gate (as typed, or its catalogue-resolved number — see gsx-gate-resolved), preceded by an 'arrival-gate-dispatched' event (trigger auto|sendNow|restore|atc) and the GSX 'Gate request <gate>: Armed' line.

fail: the flight lands with the gate confirmed/restored and NO 'arrival-gate-dispatched' event in any of its sessions — the queue never fired (the pre-#102 signature: 'Arrival gate A05 confirmed' + 'Send Now' at 13:43 in the descent, app restarted 13:51, nothing further; GSX offered 'Gate A 5' on the parking menu at 14:16).

fail: an 'arrival-gate-dispatched' event exists but no 'GSX command gate.select' line follows before touchdown while GSX was Ready and the destination was loaded (mirror airport == FMS destination) — the GSX dispatcher held the armed request; read its 'Gate request <gate>: Armed — waiting (...)' / in-flight airport pick lines (probe gsx-gate-select-failure-detail, gsx-parking-wake) for why. A send that was correctly held because GSX never loaded the destination before parking (no in-flight pick possible) is a GSX-side 'untested', reported with the pick attempts, not a fail of this probe.

assert-absent: a second 'arrival-gate-dispatched' with trigger=auto for the same gate in one session (TakeAuto fires once per queued gate) — a Cruise re-entry (step climb) or Cruise → Descent must not resend. A second dispatch after a pilot re-Confirm / Send Now, or after a restart (trigger restore), is legitimate.

When the app restarted in flight: the new session's 'arrival-gate-restored' (action + phase) and 'Arrival gate <gate> restored after restart' lines, then the dispatch per the rules above — the #102 scenario proper (confirm in the descent, restart, expect gate.select before touchdown).
probes.notes: Issue #102 (2026-08-22 EGLL→LGAV): 'A05' sent in the descent stayed armed in GsxGateSelectionService (destination not loaded), the app restarted for beta.13 and the in-memory request was gone; the coordinator's auto-fire was Cruise-only so nothing re-armed. Fixed 2026-10-09: ArrivalGatePlan.TakeAuto fires in Cruise/Descent/Approach/LandingRollout/TaxiIn (once per queued gate); the persisted queue (arrival-gate.json, since rc.3) now carries atcOrigin + flightNumber and is restored at startup; the OFP page shows a restored gate without an OFP; the coordinator records 'arrival-gate-confirmed' / 'arrival-gate-dispatched'. Unverified live. The machine block only proves 'a gate.select went out after a confirm'; the before-touchdown ordering and the restart case are the LLM checks.

checks: Only with cabin.autoAnswerGround and/or cabin.autoAnswerAir = true (both off by default). Trigger = a 'cabin.calling' event whose autoAnswer field reads Ground (phase PushbackAndStart/TaxiOut) or Air (Descent/Approach) — the cabin-secure and cabin-ready calls.

assert-present: for each such call ONE 'cabin.auto-answer' event with verdict 'answered' (the FO wrote 1 to the dataref — system.switches.S_ASP2_CAB_REC_LATCH with the default left seat, S_ASP_CAB_REC_LATCH with speech.pilotSeat = right) at least delayMs after the cabin.calling event, followed by the 'cabin.report' and the FO's '.ack' speech, then a second event with verdict 'released' (the latch written back to 0) after the report. The log line 'Cabin call auto-answer (<gate>, <phase>, after <delay> ms, <dataref>): <verdict>' pairs with each event.

verdict 'pilot-answered' (CAB was already selected, or selected during the delay) and 'mic-borrowed' (a guided dialogue held the mic) are correct no-write outcomes — report them, never as failures. 'written-no-echo' means ProSim did not echo the latch within 2 s: the write went out but the panel did not follow (a hardware ACP driving the switch is the suspect) — report with the dataref name; the report still played after the grace.

assert-absent: any 'cabin.auto-answer' event, or any write to a system.switches.S_ASP* dataref (log 'Cabin call auto-answer' / a write-gate refusal naming S_ASP), while the phase is anything other than PushbackAndStart, TaxiOut, Descent or Approach — including the boarding-delay call at the gate.
assert-absent: a 'cabin.auto-answer' event while both options are off.

requires-human: with the option on, the purser report plays after the delay without touching the ACP, the FO's acknowledgement follows, and the FO panel's CAB knob shows selected during the report and deselected after (ProSim ACP page or the hardware panel).
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-09 (issue #11, owner approval 2026-10-09; unverified live). Prosim2GSX kept the AnswerCabinCallGround/Air settings but ProsimInterface held the behaviour: it watched the real I_ASP_CAB_CALL light and pressed CAB SEND, VHF1 SEND and RESET through a MobiFlight LVAR toggle. Here the trigger is the app's own purser call (the real light is SDK read-only) and the answer is one idempotent latch write — CAB reception on the FO's panel, exactly the condition the report already waits for — released after the report. Ground window = PushbackAndStart + TaxiOut (the cabin-secure report often fires while the engines are starting; the brief said TaxiOut — widen or narrow in CabinAutoAnswer.GateFor). Allow-list: the captain's and the FO's CAB_REC_LATCH only.

checks: Trigger: the INIT page's RESET FLIGHT (SOFT) / UNLOAD OFP (FULL) buttons (second press within 3 s) or the commands efb.resetFlight / efb.unloadOfp. Behaviour: one 'efb-reset' event per press with kind soft|full, cleared[] and failed[], paired with the log line 'EFB reset: <kind> reset: cleared …' and the GSX decision 'efb reset'.

kind = soft: cleared is exactly [init-overrides, loadsheet-cycle]; NO gateway write to efb.* or aircraft.refuel.* follows other than the overrides service restoring OFP values ('EFB INIT: override … cleared — OFP value … restored'); the OFP stays on the INIT page (no 'OFP LOADED' → 'AWAITING OFP' change); no flight-cycle reset decision.

kind = full: cleared contains ofp-store, the eight datarefs in this order — efb.passengers.booked.string, efb.passengerStatistics, aircraft.refuel.fuelTarget, efb.plannedfuel, efb.plannedCargoKg, efb.simbriefPlanImported, efb.prelimLoadsheet, efb.finalLoadsheet — and flight-cycle; then the same evidence a GSX arrival reset leaves: 'loadsheet state reset for new flight cycle', 'flight cycle reset — INIT overrides cleared' (when any existed), 'Flight times' and gate-monitor resets, the pushback choice cleared. The INIT page reads AWAITING OFP afterwards.

assert-absent after a full reset: any GSX service trigger ('service.trigger' / 'gsx-service' Requested) before a new 'simbrief import: imported …' decision — the flight-plan gate must stay closed with the store empty and efb.simbriefPlanImported false. Exception: the pilot's MCDU plan still loaded opens the gate by the existing ADR-0006 rule — note it, not a failure.

failed[] non-empty (ProSim refused a write, or ProSim absent): the event still carries the app-side clears, the INIT note reads 'RESET INCOMPLETE — PROSIM REFUSED …' and the command answers failed with the names; never a silent partial reset.

requires-human: in the ProSim EFB after UNLOAD OFP the booked seat map is empty, planned fuel/cargo read 0, the W&B page shows no loadsheet, and a following FETCH OFP imports normally (the importer's 'AlreadyImported' short-circuit must not fire — the flag was cleared).
probes.notes: Shipped 2026-10-09 (owner approval; no issue number; unverified live). ProsimInterface parity: ResetFlight() = soft, UnloadOfp() = full. The full reset clears exactly the SimBrief import's write set + the two loadsheet slots (all already allow-listed, no new dataref) and raises GroundOpsSignals.FlightCycleReset — the GSX arrival's own turnaround path — so every flight-cycle store resets through its existing handler. Side effect to watch: the startup-resync's handler writes the Turnaround tracking LVAR = 1, so an app restart after a first-leg unload resyncs as a turnaround (no reposition). Not reproduced from the predecessor on purpose: cancel boarding, zeroing fuel on board / cargo holds / current seat occupation, rewriting efb.flightTimestampJSON — those move aircraft state, not the plan.

checks: watch: count the 'voice.unmatched' events per flight and group them by normalized; list every phrase heard 3+ times (suppressed = false) as a COMMAND CANDIDATE with its contexts (idle / checklist: <line> / checklist-hold / confirm-declined) and reasons — these are the phrases the pilot actually uses that the FO has no action for. The support reducer pre-computes this as sessions[].voiceUnmatched.candidates.

watch: suppressed = true events are sterile-phase absorptions (TakeoffRoll / InitialClimb / LandingRollout / short final) — count them, never list them as candidates; a large count in Cruise would mean the sterile gate misfired.
watch: context 'checklist: <line>' with reason not-an-answer = the pilot's answer to that line is not in its acceptedPhrases (an answer-phrase candidate for that checklist file, not a command).

Cross-check: every voice.unmatched event has a matching Debug line 'ASR heard "<text>" … -> Reject|Resolved' just before it; a question the handler took (an 'fo.query' event for that text) must NOT also be a voice.unmatched event.
assert-absent: a voice.unmatched event for a phrase that a feature actually handled in the same second (the same text appearing in a feature's own session event) — double-counting.
probes.notes: Issue #112, built 2026-10-09 (unverified live). UnmatchedUtteranceTracker (Speech) at every UtteranceRouter fall-through: engine reject, interpreter reject, no handler after snapping, a non-answer while a line awaits, a declined 'did you mean'. speech.trackUnmatched (default on) gates the event and the Voice page list; the ASR Debug trail is independent of it. The post-flight pass is described in docs/agents/flight-verification.md ('Voice command candidates').

checks: Trigger: a 'briefing.spoken' event while the tech log held an open item (a 'techlog.raised' / 'techlog.wear' earlier with no 'techlog.rectified' for that id, or the Tech Log page shows it open) and techLog.briefOpenItemsInBriefings = true. Behaviour: a 'techlog.consulted' event with source departure-briefing just before the departure's briefing.spoken, items[] naming the open titles (max 3 named in the narrative, the rest as 'and N more'), and the briefing narrative (templated or LLM) containing 'tech log' and the first title.

Arrival: a 'techlog.consulted' with source arrival-briefing ONLY when an open item is MEL category A/B or about brakes/gear/spoilers/reversers/autobrake/anti-skid; a clean or cabin-only log at arrival means NO arrival event (report as pass-by-absence when the trigger was a cabin-only item).

Checklist: with techLog.flagChecklistItems = true, a 'checklist.voice' start for a checklist holding a tagged line (system = apu/gear/autobrake/…) while a matching item is open yields ONE 'techlog.consulted' with source checklist, checklist, item, system and items[] — and the matching 'speech.segment'/arbiter utterance for that line ends with 'note, open tech log item: <title>.' A second tagged line about the same system in the same run, and a say-again, produce no second event.

assert-absent: a techlog.consulted event while techLog.enabled = false or the matching switch is off; a checklist.voice.item result that changed because of the note (the line's verification is untouched).
Number verifier: no 'Briefing number verification failed' warning whose unverified token comes from a tech-log title (titles' digits are in the allowed set).
probes.notes: ROADMAP 'Tech-log procedural hooks', built 2026-10-09 (unverified live). TechLogConsultation (Core, pure): departure = every open item, arrival = category A/B or landing keywords, checklist = line system tag vs the item's System field or a whole word of its title. BriefingComposer appends the 'tech-log' NarrationSection after every existing clause and lists the items in the LLM fact block; SpokenChecklistEngine.SpeakChallenge appends the note once per item per run.

checks: Only with speech.regionFacts.enabled = true (off by default). Trigger = a cruise of at least the shortest gap (default 15 min) over a country or a named sea.

assert-present: 'fo.region-fact' events with outcome 'spoken', each carrying regionKey (ISO code such as FR, or sea:<name>), region, source ('model' | 'curated'), text, lat/lon and countThisFlight; phase is Cruise on every one. The log line 'Region fact (<source>) for <region>: ...' matches each. The regionKey must agree with the lat/lon on the event — a fact about France at 52N 5E is a failure.

assert-absent: two 'spoken' events with the same regionKey in one flight (the no-repeat rule); more 'spoken' events than speech.regionFacts.maxPerFlight (default 4); two 'spoken' events closer together than minIntervalMinutes; any fo.region-fact event in a phase other than Cruise; any 'speech.spoken' with tag fo.region-fact while the mic pill read PAUSED, in a sterile phase, or after a 'smalltalk.silenced' event.

assert-absent: with speech.regionFacts.enabled = false, any 'fo.region-fact' event at all; the log holds exactly one 'Region facts disabled (speech.regionFacts.enabled)' line per start (zero log noise beyond it).

watch: outcome 'unresolved' (open water the atlas does not name, e.g. the North Atlantic) and 'no-position' — count them; 'repeated' is normal on a long leg inside one country. Outcome 'no-fact' = the model was up but said nothing and the curated file had no entry for that regionKey — list the keys so the seed file can grow.

source 'model' only when the LLM was on and healthy (llm.stream events of kind fo.region-fact precede it); source 'curated' otherwise, and always when speech.regionFacts.llmFacts = false. A 'model' fact never contains a figure next to a flight-data word (the #153 guard refuses the sentence; a refusal shows as the llm.stream takeover with the curated fact spoken instead).
requires-human: the fact is true of the place below and reads as a passenger-tone aside, not a briefing; a curated fact with the persona on is spoken in the persona's voice with the same figures.
probes.notes: Feature 2026-10-09 (issue #122, feature/cruise-immersion; unverified live). RegionFactCore (pure scheduler: jittered gap min..max, per-flight cap, no repeat per region, re-arm with the cabin latches) + RegionFactService (30 s tick; atlas lookup via IPlaceLookup from #153; model tier through StreamingNarrator under the ChatSentenceAllowed guard, VerifyNumbers off like every trivia path; curated tier = region-facts.json in %LOCALAPPDATA%\ProsimCompanion\config, seeded from {app}\config, persona-restyled with figures locked). Low priority, tag fo.region-fact, IsStillValid = still in Cruise and ear not paused. Decision: the model is the preferred tier when up (variety), the curated file the floor.

checks: Only with cabin.cruiseQuery = true (off by default) and cabin.enabled. Trigger = a cruise longer than cabin.cruiseQueryDelayMinutes (default 10, jittered +/-30 %) with the flight live.

assert-present: exactly ONE 'cabin.cruise-query' event per flight (text, windowSeconds, freeForm, phase = Cruise), preceded by 'cabin.calling' with report cabin.cruise-query, then exactly one 'cabin.cruise-reply' (heard, kind in silence|eta|ride|eta+ride|generic, ack). The log lines 'Purser cruise query: ...' and 'Purser cruise reply: <kind> ("<heard>") -> "<ack>"' match. The two speech.spoken items carry tag cabin.cruise-query and role Purser.

assert-present: kind matches what was said — 'about forty minutes' / 'on time' / 'ten minutes late' => eta; 'smooth' / 'light chop' / 'expect turbulence' => ride; both in one breath => eta+ride; anything else => generic; nothing => silence with the no-reply line. A reply read as the wrong kind is a classifier failure: quote heard + kind.

assert-absent: a second cabin.cruise-query in the same flight (the once-per-flight latch; a new flight = ColdAndDark or a Preflight after Shutdown/TaxiIn); a cabin.cruise-query outside Cruise; one while the mic pill read PAUSED; a 'speech.spoken' for the query text with IsStillValid dropped (outcome Dropped) — the question must not be asked after a descent began.
assert-absent: any dataref write, GSX call, radio or MCDU action in the seconds after the reply — the reply is acknowledged only, never acted on.

watch: 'Purser cruise query deferred — another dialogue owns the microphone' means the latch was handed back and the call retried a minute later; count the deferrals. freeForm = false means the offline engine was active and the window carried the closed reply grammar — note whether the pilot's reply was heard at all.

requires-human: the chime, then the purser's question in the purser voice after CAB was selected (or the grace); the listening tone; the acknowledgement that fits the answer; a running spoken checklist held and resumed untouched around the window.
probes.notes: Feature 2026-10-09 (ROADMAP open item 'Purser cruise query + response window', feature/cruise-immersion; unverified live). CabinCrewCore arms the once-per-flight latch on the first cruise tick (delay = minutes x (0.7 + 0.6 x roll)), fires on the first cruise tick at/after it with the ear on; CabinCrewService runs the chime + CAB latch-or-grace flow, then CabinCruiseQueryDialogue borrows the mic (IMicOwnership) for cabin.cruiseQueryWindowSeconds (default 20) — empty grammar (free-form) when the LAN transcriber is active, CabinCruiseQueryCore.OfflineGrammar otherwise — and CabinCruiseQueryCore classifies the reply by whole-word keyword lists. Predecessor Prosim2FO asked about the weather ahead with an 8 s window and a probability roll; this design asks about the arrival time / turbulence after a delay, once per flight, no roll.

checks: Only with gsx.deice.autoRequest = ask or auto (off by default — with off, the one 'gsx-deice-policy' verdict per departure reads Off and nothing else below applies). Trigger = the departure sequence started at the gate (gsx-decision 'departure sequence: started' / 'auto-started') with an OFP origin and ProSim OAT (or a METAR temperature) available.

assert-present: a 'gsx-deice-policy' event per departure cycle whose verdict is one of NoData | NotRequired | Ask | Request and whose reason names the OAT figure, its source ('ProSim OAT' or '<ICAO> METAR') and the threshold; oat/precip/icao match the Flight Status local weather card (precip in none | rain | snow | thunderstorm | freezing precipitation | ice pellets / hail | freezing fog | unknown) and the gsx-decision 'de-ice policy' line carries the same text.

Verdict rules to check against the METAR in the same session: OAT above the threshold ⇒ NotRequired whatever the METAR; at/below with snow, FZRA/FZDZ, PL/GR/GS, rain, FZFG, or a temperature/dew-point spread ≤ 3 ⇒ Ask (mode ask) / Request (mode auto); at/below with a dry METAR and a wide spread ⇒ NotRequired; at/below with NO METAR for the origin and requirePrecipitation=true ⇒ NoData (and never a request). A Request/Ask on a warm or dry day is a failure to quote.

Ask mode: after the Ask verdict a 'deice-question' event with the prompt (speech pillar; the FO speaks it, speech.spoken tag) and then one 'gsx-deice-policy' event with verdict accepted | declined and source voice | web | called | timeout; the gsx-decision 'de-ice question' line matches. While the question stands the Status board holds DeIce with 'waiting for the captain's answer — conditions call for de-icing' (gsx-decision 'hold DeIce') and Boarding is NOT held by it (its hold reason, if any, is its own activation rule).

Auto mode or an accepted question: the sequencer trigger 'DeIce' goes out LAST (gsx-decision 'trigger'/slot lines for DeIce after Boarding's Completed edge; the service-trigger wire command for DeIce follows every other departure service), then the GSX DeIce lifecycle edges (Requested/Active/Completed) and the existing deice-completed → holdover-card path. A DeIce trigger before boarding completed, with the step not configured by the pilot, is a failure.

Declined (voice 'negative', web 'No de-icing', or timeout after 5 min with no answer): gsx-decision 'skip DeIce' reads 'de-icing declined: …' when a DeIce step was configured, and 'gsx-departure-complete' follows without any DeIce trigger. assert-absent: a departure that never completes because the de-ice question was never answered (no 'gsx-departure-complete' with a standing 'hold DeIce' older than 5 min).

watch: 'gsx-deice-state' events — the first live values of L:FSDT_GSX_DEICING_STATE. Record every (previousState → state, fluidType) pair with the DeIce lifecycle edge nearest in time; the expected table is 1 Callable / 4 Requested / 5 Active / 6 Completed and the doc (docs/integrations/gsx.md §2) is updated from what was seen. A state 6 arriving BEFORE the Remote API Completed edge is the case for arming the holdover card from the LVAR.

assert-absent: the log line 'De-ice policy evaluation failed' and more than three 'de-ice policy' decision lines per departure with the same verdict (the reason uses whole degrees so a drifting OAT must not re-log).

probes.title: The FO never answers its own voice heard back from the speakers
checks: assert-absent: a fo.query whose question (normalised) shares 60 % or more of its words with the text of a fo.answer or speech.spoken event in the previous 30 s — that is the FO answering itself (2026-10-10: a VBAN loop put the FO on the cockpit speakers; 23 queries in 90 s, every one a line the FO had just said).

assert-present (when bleed happened): asr.self-echo events, each text matching a recent speech.spoken / fo.answer text — the second guard caught what the mic gate missed; count them and note the audio routing that let the FO reach the mic.

watch: log lines `ASR mic ignored while the FO speaks (episode N)` at Debug — one per FO line is normal; none at all while the FO spoke with the mic open means the SpeechStatusStore watch is not wired.
watch: pilot commands spoken right after an FO line that were NOT heard (nothing in asr.utterance within the tail) — if common, speech.micTailAfterSpeakingMs (700) is too long for that cockpit.
probes.notes: Fix 2026-10-10 (no issue number): LanAsrRecognizer ignores the mic while SpeechStatusStore.NowPlaying is set and for speech.micTailAfterSpeakingMs after (segmenter Reset on entry), and drops a transcript whose words are ≥ 60 % contained in a line spoken in the last 30 s (SelfEchoGuard, session event asr.self-echo). Both behind speech.muteMicWhileSpeaking (on). Never flown.
